newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil rate cut shows policy continuity - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Brazil rate cut shows policy continuity - cenbank.

text.p: A cut in December's Basic Interest Rate of the Central Bank (TBC) to 1.74 percent from 1.78 percent in November is a signal to the market of policy continuity, said the bank's chief Gustavo Loyola.
Loyola told reporters it showed Brazil would continue to pursue a policy of gradual interest rate cuts.

Loyola also said a decision to keep the Rate of Assistance of the Central Bank (TBAN) level in December from November at 1.90 percent was aimed at reducing the need for Central Bank intervention and assistance to the banking sector.
Loyola said that by expanding the difference between the interest rate floor (TBC) and ceiling (TBAN), banks would resort less to rediscount lines charged at the higher TBAN rate.
The Central Bank chief added that he foresaw a continued drop in interest rates because the government saw no need to alter its monetary policy.
